title: Analyst, Finance
description:
About the Role

The Finance Analyst plays a critical support role within MEI’s Debt Finance function, coordinating financing due diligence across MEI’s portfolio of renewable energy assets. This role is responsible for maintaining transaction data rooms, tracking lender and lender’s counsel requirements, and ensuring project information moves efficiently from collection through funding. Working cross-functionally with Development, Real Estate, Legal, Engineering, Construction, and Asset Management — as well as external parties such as surveyors, developers, contractors, and consultants — the Finance Analyst keeps financing workstreams organized, on schedule, and audit-ready. This is a highly cross-functional, process-oriented role suited to someone who is organized, detail-driven, and comfortable managing multiple moving pieces at once.

What You’ll Own

  • Due Diligence Management – Prepare, populate, and maintain debt financing due diligence checklists for lender’s counsel review; track lender and lender’s counsel comments, questions, and diligence requests through resolution, coordinating required responses and curative actions.
  • Data Room & Documentation – Organize, upload, and maintain documents within transaction data rooms, ensuring proper indexing, version control, and completeness and integrity of project information across diligence trackers, data rooms, and financing submissions.
  • Financing Deliverables – Evaluate, prepare, draft, and compile legal exhibits, certifications, schedules, and other deliverables required for debt financings.
  • Stakeholder Coordination – Serve as a liaison between the Debt Finance team and internal stakeholders (Development, Real Estate, Legal, Engineering, Construction, Asset Management) and external parties (surveyors, developers, contractors, consultants), driving curative actions and closing out open diligence items.
  • Pipeline Tracking & Reporting – Monitor and track the status of financing workstreams across the pipeline, and prepare regular status reports on diligence progress, outstanding items, and funding readiness.

What Will Help You Succeed

(You don’t need to check every box, but here’s what will help you thrive.)

  • Bachelor's degree; coursework or experience in environmental science, public policy, finance, or commercial transactions preferred
  • 0-2 years of relevant experience
  • Familiarity with cloud-based data rooms and diligence tracking tools preferred (e.g., SharePoint, Dropbox, Smartsheet); proficiency with AI platforms preferred (e.g., Claude, Copilot)
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and proactive; able to work independently and across functions with a high degree of flexibility and resourcefulness
  • Excellent organizational and communication skills; strong attention to detail and record-keeping
  • Prior experience or relevant coursework in finance, real estate, or transactional law preferred; demonstrated interest in renewable energy financing transactions

Benefits

  • PTO and company holidays
  • Medical, dental, vision
  • Employer-paid short-term disability, long-term disability, life insurance
  • 401(k) and company match
  • Professional development stipend
  • Strong culture of collaboration, performance, and personal growth
$70,000 - $80,000 a year
The actual salary offered may vary depending on job-related factors including, but not limited to knowledge, skills, experience and location.

How We Work

At Madison Energy Infrastructure, we believe in the power of clean energy infrastructure to drive real impact—for our customers, our partners, and the communities we serve. We’ve quickly emerged as a preeminent developer, investor, and operator of distributed generation, helping organizations across sectors meet their energy goals with certainty, speed, and trust. Our robust portfolio consists of over half a gigawatt of clean energy infrastructure projects across more than 25 states.
We’re building a team that thrives on ownership and ambition. As we expand into direct, end-to-end services for Fortune 500 companies, public entities, and nonprofits alike, we rely on collaborative thinkers who bring structure to complexity, energy to execution, and curiosity to every challenge.
Our environment is fast-paced and outcome-oriented—but grounded in the belief that how we work together matters as much as what we deliver. If you’re excited to shape the future of clean energy and be part of a high-performance, high-integrity team, we’d love to meet you.

title: Coordinator, People & Workplace Ops
description:
About the Role

The Coordinator, People & Workplace Ops is a foundational role for someone early in their career who wants broad exposure, meaningful responsibility, and the chance to learn how a growing business operates from the inside. You'll sit at the center of MEI's employee experience and help build the connective tissue that keeps people connected to one another and to MEI — all while getting direct exposure to talent acquisition, people operations, workplace operations, and executive support.

This is a highly visible, high-touch role. You'll be responsible not just for making the day-to-day run exceptionally well, but for anticipating needs, connecting dots, and finding smarter ways to work as MEI grows. It's a strong fit for someone who's equally comfortable executing the details and thinking beyond them — proactive, resourceful, and eager to build a foundation that opens doors to broader responsibilities at MEI over time.

NOTE: This is an in-person role based in our Tysons Corner office, with remote coordination supporting our Richmond and Charlottesville offices. This role will be expected to travel periodically for office and team support in VA and NYC.

Employee Experience & Talent Support

  • Fluent in using AI and modern productivity tools to work smarter – thoughtfully uses technology to research, synthesize information, improve communications, streamline workflows, and automate repetitive work, while applying sound judgment around accuracy, confidentiality, and when human involvement matters
  • Intellectually curious, resourceful, and quick to learn – asks thoughtful questions, seeks to understand “the why,” and can take an ambiguous ask, figure out what needs to happen and drive it forward
  • Thrives in a fast-moving environment with competing priorities – context-switches effectively, juggles multiple workstreams, and moves fluidly between detailed execution and the bigger picture without sacrificing follow-through
  • Strong interpersonal instincts, reads people well and takes pride in handling every interaction with care

title: Performance Engineer
description:
About You

We are seeking an experienced, data-driven Performance Engineer to selectively analyze and manage the performance of our growing portfolio of over 600 solar and BESS assets across the United States. You will report directly to the Senior Manager of Analytics & Asset Management, working alongside a small team of monitoring analysts that serve as the operational intelligence layer for the entire organization.

Approximately 70% of your time will be spent identifying underperformance by interpreting production and weather data, trend analysis, quantifying energy losses, and coordinating with Regional Asset Managers (RAMs) to drive resolution. The remaining 30% focuses on admin work like the digital onboarding of new sites into our analytics ecosystem—ingesting pro-formas and PVSyst models, validating AlsoEnergy Advanced Site Configurations, and assessing as-built drawings to ensure every site is set up correctly from day one. You will work daily inside our Power BI dashboards, internal monitoring systems, Snowflake data tables, and DAS platforms (AlsoEnergy, SolarEdge, SCADA) to surface insights that protect revenue and improve fleet health.

This is a role for someone who can look at a site producing at 85% Performance Ratio and immediately start asking the right questions: Why is a site underperforming if all inverters are operational? A soiling issue? A weather anomaly? A data gap? If you thrive on pattern recognition, root-cause investigation, and translating data into action—this is your role.

About Us

We’re one of the fastest-growing solar asset owners in the country. We manage hundreds of commercial and industrial solar sites across the U.S. We believe that the people in the field, in the weeds, and in the office deserve just as much respect as the folks in the boardroom. We’re serious about performance, safety, and world-class operations of our solar and battery fleet.

Key Responsibilities

Performance Analysis & Underperformance Detection (50%)

  • Analyze weekly, and monthly production data across ~600+ solar and BESS sites using Power BI dashboards and monitoring systems. You will not be monitoring every site, you will be looking for trends that our monitoring analysts didn’t catch.
  • Evaluate key performance metrics including Performance Ratio (PR), Weather-Adjusted PR, insolation gap, availability, capacity factor, and forecast-vs-actual variance to assess site health.
  • Investigate root causes of underperformance—distinguishing between equipment failures, inverter outages, soiling/snow loss, weather anomalies, curtailment, and data quality issues.
  • Flag confirmed underperformance to the appropriate Regional Asset Manager with clear, concise summaries of the issue, affected capacity, estimated performance loss, and recommended next steps.
  • Monitor sub-inverter-level performance across the fleet to detect issues, string-level degradation, and equipment-specific trends that site-level metrics may obscure.
  • Track and follow up on open issues to ensure timely resolution
  • Contribute to monthly production reporting, including data validation, cleaning flags, and variance commentary.

Reporting & Data Insights (20%)

  • Support weekly and monthly reporting workflows.
  • Prepare variance analyses comparing actual production against P50/P75 forecasts (Models) and flag sites trending below expectations.
  • Analyze weather data (POA irradiance, GHI, Solcast actuals) alongside production to separate weather-driven shortfalls from controllable losses.
  • Document recurring underperformance patterns and contribute to the team’s institutional knowledge base for fleet-wide trend analysis.

Administration & Data Organization (30%)

  • Digitally onboard new sites into the analytics ecosystem as they reach operations, ensuring all performance baselines are established.
  • Ingest and validate pro-forma and PVSyst energy models, mapping expected production, degradation assumptions, and design parameters into the ecosystem
  • Validate AlsoEnergy Advanced Site Configuration (ASC) files against as-built drawings and equipment schedules—confirming inverter counts, string configurations, meter assignments, and sensor mappings are accurate.
  • Assess and ingest as-built electrical drawings (single-lines, string layouts, combiner maps) to build a complete digital representation of each site’s equipment hierarchy, and identify/flag discrepancies between design documents, ASC configurations, and actual DAS data feeds—coordinating corrections with the DAS provider or O&M team before the site enters active monitoring.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years of expert-level experience in commercial and utility solar monitoring using DAS/SCADA platforms (AlsoEnergy or Power Factors strongly preferred, not residential platforms like Enphase and SolarEdge that lack electrical production details needed for advanced analysis).
  • Deep understanding of solar performance metrics: Performance Ratio, availability, capacity factor, insolation, degradation, and inverter-level diagnostics.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret production and weather data to identify underperformance, distinguish equipment issues from environmental factors, and quantify energy losses.
  • Experience reading and interpreting PVSyst models, pro-forma energy projections, single-line diagrams, and string layout drawings.
  • 1+ year of experience using Power BI preferred.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel and the broader Microsoft suite.
  • Excellent written English; capable of writing clear, professional issue summaries and email communications.
  • Demonstrated critical thinking: ability to look at a dataset and identify what’s wrong before being told.
  • Enjoys structured , detail-driven work with consistent daily patterns—perfect for someone who enjoys clear routines and predictable execution.
  • Comfortable operating independently with minimal instruction.
  • Organized, detail-obsessed, and proactive about solving problems before they grow.
  • Willingness to work U.S. Eastern hours, including occasional weekends.

Technical Setup Requirements

Because this is a fully remote role, we require the following:

  • Personal computer (2022 or newer) with minimum specs: Intel i5/Ryzen 5 or better, 8GB RAM minimum, 256GB SSD
  • Hardwired primary internet connection + cellular backup (minimum +10 Mbps, <20 ms ping).
  • External monitor and headset
  • Familiarity with Zoom, Slack, Outlook, Teams, Dropbox, Adobe, and Google Suite

Compensation & Perks

  • Base pay: 50,000–75,000 PHP/month after taxes and fees
  • Stipends: USD $60/month healthcare stipend + USD $40/month internet stipend (tax deductible)
  • US holiday calendar
  • 50-hour workweek:
    • Monday–Friday 8am–6pm ET with 1-hour lunch
    • Weekends as needed (<25% of weekends, around 2-3 hours per day)

Employment Logistics

  • EOR Arrangement – Employment is facilitated through Multiplier.com, an employer of record (EOR) platform that ensures compliance with local employment laws and regulations in the Philippines
  • Payroll – Paychecks are issued by Multiplier after withholding local taxes, paid semi-monthly
  • 13th Month Pay – Handled by Multiplier as required by local law
  • Currency Conversion – Madison covers the cost of currency conversion
  • Time Tracking – You will use Multiplier's built-in timesheet portal

How We Work

We’ve quickly emerged as a preeminent developer, investor, and operator of distributed generation, helping organizations across sectors meet their energy goals with certainty, speed, and trust. Our robust portfolio consists of over half a gigawatt of clean energy infrastructure projects across more than 25 states.
We’re building a team that thrives on ownership and ambition. As we expand into direct, end-to-end services for Fortune 500 companies, public entities, and nonprofits alike, we rely on collaborative thinkers who bring structure to complexity, energy to execution, and curiosity to every challenge.
Our environment is fast-paced and outcome-oriented—but grounded in the belief that how we work together matters as much as what we deliver. If you’re excited to shape the future of clean energy and be part of a high-performance, high-integrity team, we’d love to meet you.

title: Senior Director, Digital Infrastructure Partnerships
description:
The Role

Coming on the heels of Madison Energy Infrastructure’s pledge to develop 1 GW / $2Bn of Community Infrastructure by 2028, we are seeking to make a critical hire to lead and own partnerships with digital infrastructure customers and partners (Aggregators, Hyperscalers, Edge Data Centers, and other large power users in the digital space). This pivotal person will report directly to the Chief Development Officer and be responsible for securing the crucial partnerships and investment-grade offtake — at an acceptable price and term, for a specified volume — that will allow MEI to meet its ambitious Community Infrastructure goals.

Working closely with Development, Origination, Commercial Analysis, Regulatory/Policy, Legal, and the MEI Executive Team, the Senior Director will own the evolution of partnerships and customer relationships from the first conversation, into memorandum of understanding and exclusivity, and into binding commercial agreements. This is a partnership-oriented role built on durable, high-trust relationships where success is measured through executed term sheets and binding agreements that convert into megawatts under contract.

As part of our Community Infrastructure announcement, we defined a new goal to Build Here, Benefit Here whereby we are attempting to partner with local communities, utilities, government agencies, etc. to listen to their concerns with power/data center development and develop our projects in ways that benefit local communities. This person will be critical in coordinating that story with the community benefits teams at Digital Infrastructure Companies and at times also acting as the face of our efforts in those local communities.

This role is ideal for a self-directed commercial dealmaker who is comfortable working partnerships and attending conferences independently, can tactically and respectfully hold firm in customer/partner negotiation, and has keen sense of where to spend time and who to spend it with. Deep existing relationships within and understanding of the power demands of digital infrastructure is a must.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full partnership lifecycle with Digital Infrastructure customers (Aggregators, Hyperscalers, Edge Data Centers, and other large power users) — from first conversation through MOU/exclusivity to binding commercial agreements, including drafting, negotiating, and executing MOUs, LOIs, PPAs, and other investment-grade offtake documents.
  • Structure deals that work for both sides: partner with Commercial Analysis, Legal, and Regulatory/Policy to ensure terms are financeable, legally sound, and feasible under evolving market structures, bringing in new deal structures where needed to support Community Infrastructure build-out.
  • Lead community benefit coordination for Digital Infrastructure partnerships — working with partners' community benefit teams and serving as MEI's local representative to communities, utilities, and government agencies as part of the Build Here, Benefit Here commitment.
  • Represent MEI externally at key industry conferences and bring market intelligence back to the internal strategy team — competitors, pricing, programs — to sharpen how MEI prioritizes and sizes digital infrastructure opportunities.
  • Maintain accurate pipeline, counterparty, and deal-stage data in Salesforce as the system of record for this partnership portfolio.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree, with coursework or experience in business, economics, engineering, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in business development/origination in distributed solar, storage, digital infrastructure or comparable infrastructure transactions, with demonstrated execution of binding transactions for dozens if not hundreds of MWs of power supply and/or power demand.
  • Deep knowledge of and relationships in the digital infrastructure space, you should be able to distinguish what is a must-have vs. a nice-to-have in a data center power supply transaction.

Preferred

  • Experience in PJM markets, and familiarity with state distributed generation programs (Illinois, Maryland, Ohio, New York, Virginia).
  • Familiarity with battery energy storage transactions.
  • Knowledge of key ISO/RTO, State, and utility-level programs and regulations.
  • Comfortable using artificial intelligence tools and capable of building agents to perform specific tasks.
  • Fluency with Salesforce and deal-tracking tools.

What We Value

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a strong sense of ownership and accountability
  • Commercial lens on partnership cultivation
  • Collaborative, cross-functional approach
  • Intellectual rigor and attention to detail
  • Genuine passion for advancing renewable energy and modernizing the U.S. grid
  • Ability to operate amid competing direction from multiple senior stakeholders across the organization and prioritize based on business impact.

Benefits

  • PTO and company holidays
  • Medical, dental, vision
  • Employer-paid short-term disability, long-term disability, life insurance
  • 401(k) and company match
  • Professional development stipend
  • Strong culture of collaboration, performance, and personal growth

title: Solar & Energy Storage Estimator
description:
About the Role

As a Solar & Energy Storage Estimator on our Development team, you’ll prepare detailed cost estimates and support the technical and financial evaluation of solar PV and battery energy storage (BESS) projects, including augmentation strategies. Working closely with engineering, development, and procurement teams, you’ll contribute to project optimization and help Madison bring competitive, well-structured bids to market. This role offers direct impact on project execution and meaningful exposure across the full project lifecycle.

What You’ll Own

  • Cost Estimation – Develop detailed cost estimates for solar PV and BESS projects; maintain cost databases and estimating tools to support accuracy and consistency
  • Technical Analysis – Analyze project drawings, specifications, and proposals; interpret engineering documents to identify scope and cost drivers
  • BESS Optimization – Support BESS optimization work including augmentation strategy development and lifecycle cost analysis
  • Bid & Procurement Management – Manage and conduct EPC bid processes using Procore; solicit and evaluate vendor and subcontractor pricing; assist in bid preparation and RFP responses
  • Value Engineering – Identify value engineering opportunities and track market pricing trends to inform competitive positioning
  • Cross-Team Collaboration – Partner with engineering, development, and procurement teams to support project development and execution

  • 1–5 years of relevant experience in solar, energy storage, or related infrastructure estimating; BESS estimating experience, including familiarity with augmentation strategies and lifecycle cost analysis (preferred)
  • Background in civil, mechanical, or electrical engineering
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings and specifications
  • Strong Excel skills and analytical ability
  • Strong communication skills; able to collaborate effectively across engineering, development, and procurement functions
  • Experience using Procore for EPC bids and familiarity with Bluebeam for estimating (preferred)
  • Exposure to ISO markets or dispatch modeling (preferred)
  • Familiarity with PVsyst or similar solar modeling tools (preferred)
  • Knowledge of EPC structures and C&I solar + storage markets (preferred)

At Madison Energy Infrastructure, we believe in the power of clean energy infrastructure to drive real impact—for our customers, our partners, and the communities we serve. We’ve quickly emerged as a preeminent developer, investor, and operator of distributed generation, helping organizations across sectors meet their energy goals with certainty, speed, and trust. Our robust portfolio consists of over half a gigawatt of clean energy infrastructure projects across more than 25 states.
We’re building a team that thrives on ownership and ambition. As we expand into direct, end-to-end services for Fortune 500 companies, public entities, and nonprofits alike, we rely on collaborative thinkers who bring structure to complexity, energy to execution, and curiosity to every challenge.
Our environment is fast-paced and outcome-oriented—but grounded in the belief that how we work together matters as much as what we deliver. If you’re excited to shape the future of clean energy and be part of a high-performance, high-integrity team, we’d love to meet you.
